children: Harvey Norman's exposure to big-ticket consumer items delay an earnings recovery at the furniture and homewares retailer, UBS analyst Shaun Cousins warns. Keeping a "neutral" rating on the stock amid support from its property portfolio, Cousins tells clients in a note that Australia-listed Harvey Norman's pretax profit so far in fiscal 2027 is tracking well below both his and consensus forecasts. He points out that like-for-like sales by its Australian franchisees have been slower than those at rival JB Hi-Fi's eponymous stores and at JB's Good Guys-branded whitegoods chain. UBS cuts its target price 11%, to 4.25 Australian dollars. Shares are at A$4.13 ahead of the open. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
